differences.what: wall head: the heavy bracketed cornice over the front; the build's walls stood 0.7 m over the first fit's 7.9 m. T-2437 re-fitted this camera to the house's heights as re-read off the 1874 engraving (the cornice's soffit 10.61 m, the principal floor 2.0 m) and the build's cornice lands within the fit's 10 px of the drawn soffit (y 36 px)

north pavilion: the north part of the front proud, its south side face shaded, round-headed windows in both storeys under moulded hoods, rising past the main cornice; the build's front is flat there and carries a two-storey canted bay. On T-2437's re-fitted camera its edges land within 9 px of the drawn ones (x 141 and 218 px against 150 and 225), both storeys' windows on the drawn ones (the upper window's foot y 77 px, the principal storey's arch top y 103 px)

bay window: a one-storey bay on the south part with pilaster strips and its own cornice; built by T-2408 as the 1874 engraving's hooded canted bay. On T-2437's re-fitted camera its south part lands at x 8 px against the drawn 5 (its north part is under the '1620' cartouche). Its height is now the sketch's: T-2444 raised the bay to the 1874 engraving's heights, and its hood's eaves land at about y 117 px against the sketch's bay cornice at y 115 px, where the build's hood top stood about 13 px (0.65 m) under it before. The pilaster strips the sketch draws on the bay's face, white between its hatched lights, built by T-2462 as the 1874 engraving places them: light painted strips 0.2 m wide down the bay's two front corners from its plinth to its hood, landing at x 26-33 px (the north one under the cartouche); the sketch draws the south strip at its bay's edge, x 7-15 px, where its freehand bay stands wider than either camera allows, within what this approximate camera can say

windows: the south part's upper window, beside the cartouche at the sketch's left edge, round-headed under a hood; built so by T-2410 (the cartouche covers the rest of the south part); T-2462 moved it to v 2.5 off the bay's centre, as the 1874 engraving draws it, and it lands at x 33-53 px against the sketch's 37-60 px, within this camera's 10 px

entrance: the stoop rising straight from the gate (x 93-140 px, about v 6.3-7.5 at the street line) to a door beside the pavilion's south face. Built (T-2409): the door moved to v 6.6, its 1.8 m stoop rising straight to it and its landing ending at the pavilion's south face; the porch before the pavilion stands behind the sketch's lattice fence and its '1620' cartouche hides the door's hood. On T-2437's camera the gate's piers land at x 71-93 and 146-168 px against the drawn 70-91 and 142-157, and the porch's head on the drawn 192 px. T-2463 moved the door 0.675 m south to v 5.925, under the window over it, as the 1874 engraving draws it, and left the stoop, its gate and its walk on v 6.6: the sketch's cartouche covers the front over the stoop's head, so it cannot say where the door stands, and its stoop still rises from the gate where the build's does

bay window's terrace: the stoop's terrace carried south before the bay (T-2450, from the 1874 engraving, which draws its turned balustrade). The sketch draws the bay's foot on a level line at about y 188-192 px over its lattice fence, where the build's terrace head lands (y 193 px), and draws no balusters before the bay, as it draws none on the porch before the pavilion (T-2409's, whose head lands on the drawn 192 px); the engraving, a true perspective that draws both balustrades baluster by baluster, is read for them over the freehand sketch, whose cartouche scroll and lattice top cross both

fence: a lattice of interlaced arches between square piers with capped tops, on a base, gate piers at the walk; built so by T-2414 (k11.fence.lattice_arcade between the kit's posts on its stone curb, the arches running on from post to post); the sketch's lattice stands taller over its base than the kit's 0.95 m rails, within what this approximate camera can say (its solve: a freehand sketch). On T-2437's camera the fence's foot lands on the drawn one (y 269 px) and its lattice's top about 15 px (0.35 m) under the sketch's (y 202 px), more than this camera's 10 px; the 1874 engraving, a true perspective, puts the lattice's top at 1.50 m and the build's within about 6 px of it, so the sketch's taller lattice is read as its draughtsman's
the roof: the panel cuts the house at the cornice
colour and walling: a pen sketch
gate: the sketch draws the flight rising straight from the gate between the piers with no leaf across it; the build's leaves were shut across the stair's foot
differences.how: T-3214: the entrance leaves drawn open 70 degrees, the flagged walk laid from the stair's foot through the gate (K14 yard)

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153).
